newsitem.title: USA: Ranger Oil ups North Sea forecasts.
newsitem.headline: Ranger Oil ups North Sea forecasts.

text.p: Canada's Ranger Oil Ltd believes that reserves at two North Sea oil fields could be substantially higher than presently believed, company chief executive Fred Dyment told a conference here on Friday.
He said that reserves at the Harding field in which Ranger has a five percent interest could be 200 million barrels and the Ninian area has at least 150 million barrels of reserves.
"We can really maximise reserves and production rates can be jacked up," Dyment said.
Ninian, in which Ranger has a 24 percent interest, produces 55,000 barrels of crude per day and Harding, where it has five percent, 80,000 barrels.
Ranger is also in the final stages of negotiation to pick up another 20 percent of the Kyle field. It bought a stake in the field last year.
Dyment also said that full development of the North Sea Banff field would come in mid 1999 with output of 60,000 barrels of oil per day, of which Ranger has 26.2 percent.
The North Sea Pierce field, in which Ranger has a 15.6 percent stake will come to full production of 45,000 barrels of crude per day in mid-1998.
He said that Ranger's Angolan operations, on which it took a $71 million one time charge last year, had seen some positive results.
"We have made one small discovery of six to eight million barrels in the Kiame field and we are in negotiations with the government to get another stake," he said.
